key_insight: The Nephro Candidate Score combines machine learning and inheritance heuristics to prioritize candidate variants and genes in suspected inherited kidney disease.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support genetic investigation by narrowing candidate lists, but prioritized findings still require validation.
method: XGBoost-based Nephro Gene Score predicts gene–disease relevance.
Logistic regression-based Nephro Variant Score predicts variant pathogenicity.
An inheritance score complements both models for candidate prioritization.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included 1,452 individuals; independent-test AUCs were 0.94 for gene relevance and 0.99 for variant pathogenicity, and 10 of 11 newly proposed kidney disease genes received high scores.
watch_item: Strong prioritization performance does not establish diagnostic accuracy or confirm ERMP1 and other highlighted candidates as disease-causing.
paper_title: Automated Variant Prioritization in Suspected Genetic Kidney Disease
